entities.name: Achille Manara
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Achille Manara (1839–1917) was an Italian Catholic bishop who served in the Italian Church during the difficult period following Italian unification. Born in Reggio Emilia, he was ordained a priest and rose through the diocesan ranks to become bishop, serving in the context of the Church-state tensions that defined Italian Catholicism in the post-Risorgimento era.

The Italian Church faced acute institutional challenges after 1870: the Law of Guarantees that sought to regulate Church-state relations was unilaterally imposed without Vatican consent; religious orders were suppressed and their properties confiscated; and Catholic political activity was restricted by the non expedit policy that discouraged Catholic participation in Italian parliamentary politics. Bishops like Manara navigated the practical challenges of maintaining Catholic institutional life under these restrictive conditions.

His long episcopate spanned the period from the most acute phase of Church-state conflict under the Kingdom of Italy to the beginning of a gradual accommodation between the Church and the Italian state that would eventually produce the Lateran Treaty of 1929. His ministry modelled the practical Catholic bishop who maintained diocesan institutions and community life despite hostile legal and political environments.
